data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Myrta is the name of a nymph who presided over gardens and groves. The name Myrta comes from the Greek word 'myrto', meaning myrtle tree. Myrta was a popular name among the ancient Greeks and Romans, and it is believed to have been used as a symbol of love and fertility. The name Myrta carries the meaning “Myrtle tree” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Myrta usually hope their child will grow to embody myrtle tree and live with faith, good character and purpose.
